rawFindings.title: Removed `_baseRoute` caching breaks multiple handlers on same route
rawFindings.explanation: The change removes the `_baseRoute` method and uses `_router.route(path)` directly every time. Previously, `_baseRoute` cached Route instances per path, which ensured multiple handlers on the same path were attached to the same Route object. After removal, each call to `app.VERB(path, ...)` calls `_router.route(path)` which may create distinct Route objects, losing existing handlers, thus breaking the ability to add multiple handlers to the same route.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the `_baseRoute` method caching Route objects and use it in the HTTP verb methods and in `app.all` to ensure the same Route instance is used per path.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Adding multiple handlers for the same path with `app.get(path, handler1)` and then `app.get(path, handler2)` results in only one handler being registered instead of both, causing requests to not invoke all expected handlers.
